notes:
SLO discussion notes and measurement alignment (CRM-style bullets):
- Customer very focused on real end-user experience not just server-only numbers. CTO: 'Our SLAs must map to the app metrics we care about — not black-box.'
- We walked through differences: server-side inference latency vs client-side end-to-end (ingress + network + first-byte + decode). Montclair wants both reported and aligned.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: agreed definitions: streaming = first-token-first-byte (TTFB) measurable per response chunk; non-streaming = single-shot completion time (time to last token). Montclair will measure p50/p95/p99 for both first-byte and completion where applicable.
- Measurement alignment decision: Redwood to provide both server-side telemetry (ingress_ts, model_start_ts, model_end_ts, egress_chunk_ts) and a client-side synthetic agent to capture network variance. We'll compare and reconcile for SLA credits.
- Tail risk: p99 amplifies when streaming due to network jitter and incremental decode. Proposed approach: report two p99 numbers — server inference p99 and client E2E p99; SLA to reference server-side p99 with reconciled E2E targets as operational guidance.
- Throughput guarantees: customer asked for sustained 250 RPS at 95th percentile throughput with >99% success. Proposal: reserved pool = 4 x H100-class GPUs (or equivalent) with autoscale burst to 8 nodes for 10-minute intervals. SE recommended workload-aware batching and KV cache to reduce token compute.
- Benchmarking plan: SE to run representative 72-hour soak test (mirrored traffic) measuring p50/p95/p99 for first-byte and completion across streaming and non-streaming modes. Need montclair-sanctioned prompt set.
- SLA terms to negotiate: uptime SLA 99.9%, latency SLA tied to server-side p95 and p99; credits for missed SLA to be defined. Montclair requests additional clause for tail-latency incidents (root-cause and mitigation within 24h).
- Quote from lead engineer: 'We need clarity on how credits are calculated — client-side spikes shouldn't immediately trigger credits if server-side is healthy.'
- Action items: Maya to deliver SLO matrix + GPU sizing doc; Jordan to loop in legal for data residency; Montclair to provide sample production traces and traffic shape by 2026-03-12.
- Risks: internal PO timing, legal data residency objections, potential upward revision of p99 target once real-network E2E numbers come in.
pooled_latency_matrix: Definition: pX keys are percentiles computed on the selected measurement window (sliding 1h).
Server-side inference: measures only runtime between model_start_ts and model_end_ts (excludes network). Report p50/p95/p99.
Client E2E (synthetic): measures from client request send to last token received. Report p50/p95/p99 separately for streaming-first-byte and completion.
Streaming metrics: capture first-byte p50/p95/p99, per-chunk mean latency, and completion p95/p99 for full response length.
Non-streaming metrics: capture completion latency p50/p95/p99 and throughput (RPS).
